notes: §1985:XII.2.3 SR7: 'A COPY statement may be specified in the source program anywhere a character-string or a separator, other than the closing quotation mark, may occur except that a COPY statement must not occur within a COPY statement.' CopyProcessor#FindStatementKeyword finds COPY as any text-word (never inside a literal or comment) wherever it stands, and ExpandCopiesOneLevel splices it; ParseCopyStatement, ReadCopyName and ReadOperand refuse a COPY word as an operand, inside pseudo-text, or after the operands (COBOL2451), and at --std 85 ResolveOneCopy refuses library text that holds a COPY (COBOL0900, §1985:XII.2.4 GR12; accepted from 2002). Probes at 85: COPY in the identification division (PROGRAM-ID), the configuration section, a PICTURE clause ('PIC COPY PICX. VALUE'), and mid-statement ('ADD COPY ONE. TO N') expand and run (A=AB N=3); COPY inside a literal and a continued literal stays literal text; COPY as library-name, in pseudo-text-1, twice, and after the text-name refused COBOL2451; COPY as a word operand refused COBOL7006; nested library COPY refused at 85, runs at 2002. The witness is COPY inside pseudo-text-2.

next.reason: 1985 allows COPY 'in the source program' wherever a character-string or separator other than the closing quotation mark may occur, never within a COPY statement, and its amended GR12 says the text produced by COPY 'must not contain a COPY statement'. §2023:7.2.3.3 SR1 allows COPY 'anywhere in source text or in library text' (closing delimiter of a literal is the newer term); §2023:7.2.3.4 GR12 lets library text contain a COPY without REPLACING (nesting of at least 5 levels) and GR10 bars it when REPLACING is specified. Nested COPY, refused in 1985, is accepted. Looser.
